chapter: The Los Angeles music scene in the early 1930s
title: Sonny Clay Plantation Orchestra personnel
summary: Redd names the musicians on the Sonny Clay record date; Blakeney recalls Fitzgerald as a pianist and little about William Calhoun.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Mr. Blakeney, your first recording experiences out West was with the Sonny Clay Plantation Orchestra; this we do know. In that orchestra were people like W.B. Woodland, Ernest Coycault, Leonard "Big Boy" Davidson, Louis Dobbs; some gentleman whose last name was Fitzgerald--do you recall his first name? He was a banjo player.
I don't remember him much as a banjo player, mostly on the

Oh? We had him listed here as being a banjo player, but perhaps he was a piano. There were also other musicians on the date with you at the time, such as William Calhoun and W. B. Woodman, who was the father of Coney and Britt Woodman. Britt Woodman was a fine tromonist who played for many years with Duke Ellington, and who at this time I believe is active in New York.
Tell us a little bit about the lesser known musicians, maybe like William Calhoun. He was a multi-reed player, right?
Can you recall much about Mr. Calhoun?
